patient_overview.name: Norman Luettgen
patient_overview.description: Norman Luettgen is a 39-year-old divorced father of three living in Newark, NJ, who works full-time in a role that keeps him deskbound and often away from home at mealtimes. He comes in for a nutrition visit tied to his prediabetes, mild anemia, and an AUDIT-C score flagging risky drinking, though he presents as composed, articulate, and guarded about the drinking piece. He's done his homework online about HbA1c and insulin resistance and wants one specific, concrete change to start with rather than a lecture. He tends to answer the student's questions with his own questions, sizing up whether they actually know what they're talking about before he opens up.

demographics.occupation: IT systems administrator for a hospital network
demographics.cultural_context: Norman grew up in Newark in a working-class household where eating out was a treat reserved for birthdays; now, as a divorced father juggling custody of three kids and a demanding on-call job, takeaway and restaurant meals have become his default rather than an indulgence. He values self-sufficiency and doesn't like appearing to need help, which shapes both his guardedness about his drinking and his preference for solving problems with information rather than conversation.

medical_history: Application of composite dental filling material to dentin of tooth following fracture of tooth (2021-03-11)
Removal of subgingival plaque and calculus from all teeth using dental instrument (2021-03-11)
current_symptoms: Occasional mid-afternoon energy crashes he attributes to 'just being tired'
Mild shortness of breath climbing the stairs at his apartment that he's noticed more this year
Nasal congestion and post-nasal drip that flares a few times a month
Feels he needs a nap most Sunday afternoons
clinical_findings: Mild pallor of the conjunctiva consistent with his anemia
Noticeable nasal congestion with some mouth-breathing during conversation
Waist appears carrying weight centrally, consistent with his BMI and recent weight gain

supplements_and_otc: Over-the-counter saline nasal spray for sinus flares
A multivitamin he buys at the Rite Aid near his apartment, taken inconsistently
Occasionally takes an iron supplement a friend recommended, 'when I remember'

nutrition_profile.dietary_pattern: Heavy reliance on restaurant and takeaway meals; limited home cooking
food_preferences: Jamaican jerk chicken from a spot near his job
Burgers and fries from the diner he and his buddy Marcus go to on weekends
Chinese takeaway combo plates on weeknights when he's too tired to cook
Sweetened iced tea with most meals
foods_or_behaviors_to_explore: How often beer or liquor accompanies the takeaway orders
Whether vegetables appear anywhere outside the garnish on his plate
Late dinners after long work calls that push eating past 9pm
nutrition_profile.meal_pattern: Skips or grabs a quick breakfast; irregular lunch depending on meetings; takeaway dinner most nights, often late
nutrition_profile.hydration: Drinks iced tea and soda more than water; says he 'should drink more water' but rarely does
nutrition_profile.physical_activity: Mostly sedentary desk job; occasional weekend basketball with his kids, less often than he'd like
nutrition_profile.substance_use: Reports drinking 'a few beers on weekends' but AUDIT-C score and further questioning suggest more frequent and heavier drinking than initially stated
nutrition_profile.sleep: About 6 hours on weeknights, catches up some on Sunday with a long nap

psychosocial_profile.personality: Reserved and private; controlled, measured, gives little away until he trusts the person in front of him
psychosocial_profile.communication_style: Answers questions with questions, testing whether the student knows their material before opening up; precise vocabulary, clearly well-read
goals: Get a single, concrete first step rather than a whole overhaul
Keep his A1c from crossing into diabetes range
Have more energy to keep up with his three kids on weekends
concerns: Being told to overhaul his whole life at once
Looking weak or undisciplined if the drinking topic comes up
Running out of time between work and parenting to cook
beliefs: He trusts peer-reviewed sources and reads nutrition studies himself
He believes willpower-based advice without structure doesn't work for him
He thinks his drinking is 'under control' because it's social, not solitary
motivations: Wanting to be around and functional for his kids as they grow up
Not wanting to end up on medication he associates with 'getting old fast'
Pride in being someone who solves his own problems
fears: Developing full diabetes like his uncle, who lost part of a foot
Being lectured or treated like he doesn't already know things
Admitting he can't handle something on his own
barriers: Little time or energy to cook most nights
Takeaway dinners double as his main social outlet with friends
Drinking is tied into those same social occasions, making it hard to isolate
strengths: Highly motivated once he commits to a plan
Reads and retains health information well
Has a strong support person in his neighbour Dana who checks in on him
psychosocial_profile.support_system: His neighbour and close friend Dana, who he talks to most evenings and who has started asking him pointed questions about his drinking
psychosocial_profile.readiness_to_change: Preparation stage: has already decided he wants to change something and wants one specific, concrete first step, not a general discussion

initial_information: Name, job, and that he's here because his doctor flagged his blood sugar as 'pre-diabetic'
States he eats out or orders in most nights because of his schedule
Mentions he has three kids and is divorced
discoverable_information: Describes his typical takeaway orders in detail (jerk chicken, Chinese combo plates, diner burgers)
Admits he rarely drinks water, mostly iced tea and soda
Says he's read about glycemic index and wants to know which foods actually matter
Mentions his neighbour Dana as someone who checks in on him
reluctant_information: Acknowledges he drinks 'a few beers on weekends' when asked directly about alcohol
Admits his weekend basketball with his kids happens less often than he says at first
hidden_information: Norman actually drinks most weeknights too, often 3-4 beers or a couple of mixed drinks while watching sports alone, not just 'weekends with friends' as first stated
Dana has told him directly she's worried about how much he's drinking, which stung more than he admits
He skipped his anemia follow-up labs because he didn't want to deal with another appointment

opportunities.learning_objective: Practice motivational interviewing with a patient already in the preparation stage of change
expected_discoveries: Norman has already decided he wants to act, not just contemplate
He wants one specific, actionable step rather than broad advice
possible_patient_reactions: "So what's the one thing I should actually change first? Don't give me ten."
"I've already read the general stuff, what's new here?"

opportunities.learning_objective: Elicit a more accurate alcohol history from a patient who minimizes it initially
expected_discoveries: His AUDIT-C score of 4 suggests higher-risk drinking than 'a few beers on weekends'
He drinks most weeknights, not just socially on weekends
possible_patient_reactions: "Why does that matter for my blood sugar?"
"I don't have a problem, I just unwind after work."

opportunities.learning_objective: Translate high health literacy into a workable nutrition plan rather than overwhelming the patient with more information
expected_discoveries: Norman already understands glycemic index and HbA1c conceptually
He wants practical substitutions within his existing takeaway routine, not a diet overhaul
possible_patient_reactions: "I know what fiber does, just tell me what to order instead."
"You don't need to explain insulin resistance to me, I've read the papers."

opportunities.learning_objective: Address anemia and its nutritional contributors in a patient who has disengaged from follow-up care
expected_discoveries: He hasn't repeated his anemia labs since 2021
His diet of takeaway meals may be low in iron-rich foods and vitamin C to aid absorption
possible_patient_reactions: "I figured the vitamin would handle that."
"Honestly I forgot that was even still a thing."

opportunities.learning_objective: Identify how social eating and drinking patterns are intertwined and barriers to change
expected_discoveries: Takeaway dinners and drinking are his primary social outlet
Separating the two will require finding alternative ways to socialize
possible_patient_reactions: "That's literally my social life, what else am I supposed to do?"
"Dana and I just hang out and watch the game, it's not a big thing."

assumptions: Norman has shared custody or regular weekend time with his three children
His full-time IT role allows flexible but long hours, often eating at his desk or ordering delivery
Dana is a neighbour in his apartment building who has known him for several years
optional_details: Keeps a running list of nutrition articles saved on his phone he hasn't gotten around to reading fully
Plays in a casual Sunday basketball league with his kids and a few neighbourhood dads
Has a weighted blanket he jokes helps with his 'terrible sleep schedule'
